from_idea: Akien 2026-08-19, resolving open-a-saturated-match-rate-cannot-show-efficacy: sieves measure deterministically, LLM periodic review of feedback adjusts the parameters
intent: Scheduled probes fire LLM prompts to Hex for periodic inspection of gate feedback. The sieve stays deterministic Python; what changes is what it is calibrated against. The LLM reviews accumulated feedback and proposes parameter adjustments.
why: A sieve that measures at 100% match rate cannot show efficacy — it agrees with everything. The feedback the sieve collects is where efficacy hides, but nobody reads it. Hex reviewing the feedback on a schedule closes the loop: the sieve measures, the feedback accumulates, the LLM reads the feedback, the parameters adjust, the sieve measures differently.
sub_tickets_owed: a gate collects feedback in a shape the LLM can read
a scheduled probe fires an LLM prompt to Hex with accumulated feedback
Hex proposes parameter adjustments and the gate owner approves or rejects
the adjustment lands through the gate's own door (Law 6)
distinctions_recorded: The sieve is DETERMINISTIC PYTHON ONLY. The LLM is in the parameter-adjustment loop, never in the measurement path.
This is the learns-its-gates founding intention made concrete for one gate shape.
Hex is the inference target (the M1 Studio box), not CC. CC is too expensive for periodic review.
